Let \(\lambda=2\pi n\). In polar coordinates,
\[
x^3-3xy^2=r^3\cos 3\theta,\qquad dx\,dy=r\,dr\,d\theta.
\]
Using
\[
\int_0^{2\pi}\cos(a\cos 3\theta)\,d\theta=2\pi J_0(a),
\]
we get
\[
I_n=2\pi\int_0^1 rJ_0(\lambda r^3)\,dr
=\frac{2\pi}{3}\int_0^1 t^{-1/3}J_0(\lambda t)\,dt.
\]

Now
\[
\int_0^\infty u^{-1/3}J_0(u)\,du
=2^{-1/3}\frac{\Gamma(1/3)}{\Gamma(2/3)}.
\]
Hence
\[
\int_0^1 t^{-1/3}J_0(\lambda t)\,dt
=\lambda^{-2/3}2^{-1/3}\frac{\Gamma(1/3)}{\Gamma(2/3)}
-\int_1^\infty t^{-1/3}J_0(\lambda t)\,dt.
\]
The first term contributes
\[
\frac{2\pi}{3}(2\pi n)^{-2/3}2^{-1/3}
\frac{\Gamma(1/3)}{\Gamma(2/3)}
=
\frac{\pi^{1/3}\Gamma(1/3)}{3\Gamma(2/3)n^{2/3}},
\]
which is exactly the subtracted term.

It remains to find the first endpoint correction. For large \(z\),
\[
J_0(z)=\sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi z}}\cos\left(z-\frac{\pi}{4}\right)+O(z^{-3/2}),
\]
with the error contributing only \(O(\lambda^{-5/2})\) after one integration by parts on \([1,\infty)\). Thus
\[
\int_1^\infty t^{-1/3}J_0(\lambda t)\,dt
=
\sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi\lambda}}
\int_1^\infty t^{-5/6}\cos\left(\lambda t-\frac{\pi}{4}\right)\,dt
+O(\lambda^{-5/2}).
\]
Integrating by parts,
\[
\int_1^\infty t^{-5/6}\cos\left(\lambda t-\frac{\pi}{4}\right)\,dt
=
-\frac{\sin(\lambda-\pi/4)}{\lambda}+O(\lambda^{-2}).
\]
Therefore
\[
I_n=
\frac{\pi^{1/3}\Gamma(1/3)}{3\Gamma(2/3)n^{2/3}}
+\frac{2\pi}{3}\sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi}}(2\pi n)^{-3/2}
\sin\left(2\pi n-\frac{\pi}{4}\right)
+o(n^{-3/2}).
\]
Since \(n\) is an integer,
\[
\sin\left(2\pi n-\frac{\pi}{4}\right)=-\frac1{\sqrt2}.
\]
Hence
\[
\lim_{n\to\infty}n^{3/2}
\left(
I_n-
\frac{\pi^{1/3}\Gamma(1/3)}{3\Gamma(2/3)n^{2/3}}
\right)
=
-\frac{1}{3\sqrt2\,\pi}.
\]

\[
\boxed{-\frac{1}{3\sqrt2\,\pi}}
\]
